newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Salt to raise its Matav stake.
newsitem.headline: Salt to raise its Matav stake.

text.p: Israel Salt Industries has taken an option to acquire an additional 16.24 percent of Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd from Bank Hapoalim Investment Co for 190.69 million shekels, Hapoalim said.

If Salt exercises the option by a January 7, 1997 deadline, it will hold 32.8 percent of Matav, an Israeli cable television operator, making it its biggest shareholder. Salt will pay 25 shekels a share, an 8.5 percent discount to Matav's closing share price in Tel Aviv on Tuesday.

As part of the agreement, Salt, which is controlled by the Dankner group, will sell to Hapoalim Communications, a wholly owned subsidiary of Hapolaim Investment, its 13.3 percent equity holding in Hapoalim Investments for 90.13 million shekels, or 114.5 shekels per share.
The price represents a 5.2 premium of on Hapoalim Investment's closing price in Tel Aviv on Tuesday.

Salt acquired its Poalim stake in August as part of bid to gain control of the company through shares then being sold by Bank Hapoalim via tender. Salt lost the tender to the investment bank Dovrat Shrem.
